actions.body: Intelligent systems, when faced with limited resources, must distinguish between transient difficulty and fundamental epistemic exhaustion. Research on the sunk cost effect (source-3cd9e0756c2c4cca) highlights the systematic bias toward persistence in failing courses of action. For an intelligence, this bias can be mitigated by modeling planning tasks (source-4fb70d1c1dd147da) that incorporate objective criteria for abandonment. Furthermore, broader organizational and conservation frameworks (source-c5e9e9da1ebf41eb) suggest that sustainable agendas require periodic evaluation against shifting contexts rather than rigid adherence to initial goals. Abandonment should be treated as an optimal strategy, not a failure, when the expected value of continued inquiry falls below the threshold of alternative research opportunities.
actions.lede: The sunk cost effect creates a systematic bias where intelligence persists in failing research agendas; rational abandonment requires explicit, evidence-backed decision criteria.
actions.reason: Synthesizing evidence regarding sunk cost bias and adaptive planning to provide a foundation for question abandonment criteria.
actions.title: Rational Decision Criteria for Question Abandonment
